title: African drummers and the independence of limbs
summary: Crawford says African drummers have great independence, which he had to study hard to match.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: (Unintelligible) ofay guy, I'm not going after all that, anyway, because everybody God put on this earth and created, supposed to be the same. Some have something, -- now, you go to Africa, and come the drummers, you never in your life heard such great independence like they can do in Africa. I have not had the pleasure of going to Africa, but I've (listened) and I've learned.

You get a guy, two or three guys together, and they can make the greatest contribution to swinging and independence -- (singing), had all that going. That's a natural beat. They got the beat, but they started to throwing in triplets and all
with their left hand and left foot and all that. I can do that. I had to study and study hard on it, though.

In other words, for independence. Piano players have to have independence. Their left hand is doing one thing and their right hand is doing another, and organ players, they got to contend with that foot down there. On those pedals. Piano players had to have independence.
